clusters.name: After grandfather's death, 1989–1990
clusters.reason: Around the time your grandfather died in July 1989, your mother was lying awake over money and stopped talking with your father about it. Within months, your brother's grades fell. Your mother grew calmer once back at work by early 1990. The family's anxiety shifted around a loss that mattered to the household.

clusters.name: After your mother's breast cancer diagnosis, 1994–1996
clusters.reason: Within a year of your mother being told she had breast cancer in early 1995, you developed migraines that kept you in bed, called your brother most nights, then stopped returning his calls and stopped calling home. Your family was dealing with a serious diagnosis in your mother while you moved through shifts toward and then away from your brother. The shifts in how you related pile up around this threat to your mother.
clusters.change: The period runs from when you left home for college in 1993 through early 1996, with your mother's cancer diagnosis as the change that shifted the family's balance around then.
